format: Standalone Restaurant (freestanding with drive-thru, approx. 3,000 sq ft)

invest.quote: The total investment necessary to begin operation of a Freddy's Restaurant franchise ranges from $854,834 to $1,301,000 for an In-Line Restaurant, $1,026,334 to $2,361,000 for an End-Cap Restaurant and $1,586,334 to $2,802,000 for a Standalone Restaurant. This includes $55,000 to $95,000 that must be paid to the franchisor.

fee.quote: You must pay an initial license fee in the amount of $35,000 ("License Fee") in a lump sum when you sign the License Agreement, less any applicable License Fee Deposit or Development Fee credit due under a Development Agreement.
fee.note: Freddy Simon Salute to Veterans Program: 25% reduction in the License Fee for a veteran's first Restaurant only. Construction Advisory Services: $35,000 non-refundable Advisory Fee required for the first Restaurant. Grand opening training expenses estimated $20,000 to $60,000. Development Agreement: $15,000 x number of Restaurants plus $20,000 License Fee Deposit.

royalty.quote: Royalty 5% of all Gross Receipts2 Payable the 3rd day after the end of each consecutive week during each 28-day operating period

adFund.quote: National Marketing and Advertising Fund3 0% - 3% of Gross Receipts currently, 2.5% of Gross Receipts As of October 8, 2026, 3% of Gross Receipts
adFund.note: Currently 2.5%, rising to 3% as of October 8, 2026. Cooperative advertising 0% to 2% (none established); local advertising may be required up to 2.0% of Gross Receipts.

special: Required $35,000 Construction Advisory Services fee to the franchisor for the first Restaurant (included in construction costs in Item 7). Investment excludes land purchase. Profit margin published only for End Cap/Inline franchised units (10.1% 4-Wall EBITDA), not the Standalone format.
issues: Cover In-Line high is $1,301,000 but Item 7 total says $1,302,000. Item 19 intro says 475 franchised Restaurants open the full year but Tables 3, 4 and 7 use 477. Cover 'paid to franchisor' range ($55,000 to $95,000) appears not to include the $35,000 advisory fee.
